IHrmPlatformOrganizationDashboardBudgetW.x-autobe-specification:
Computed type aggregating project budget data from hrm_platform_projects and hrm_platform_timelogs.

1. Source Tables:
   - hrm_platform_projects: provides project id, name, budget_hours, organization_id
   - hrm_platform_timelogs: provides duration_hours for actual time logged

2. JOIN Condition:
   - hrm_platform_projects.id = hrm_platform_timelogs.project_id
   - hrm_platform_projects.organization_id = {current_organization_id}

3. Aggregation:
   - actualHours: SUM(hrm_platform_timelogs.duration_hours) GROUP BY project_id
   - budgetHours: hrm_platform_projects.budget_hours (direct mapping)

4. Filtering:
   - Only include projects where budget_hours IS NOT NULL
   - Only include projects where actualHours > budget_hours (overage condition)
   - Filter by organization context from authenticated user session

5. Calculation:
   - overagePercentage: ((actualHours - budgetHours) / budgetHours) * 100
   - Round to 2 decimal places for display

6. Edge Cases:
   - If no timelogs exist for a project, actualHours = 0 (would not trigger warning)
   - If budget_hours is null, exclude from budget warnings list
   - Handle division by zero if budget_hours = 0 (should not occur due to validation)

projectId.description: Unique identifier of the project. Represents the project where the employee has logged time, mapped from the timelog's project reference.
projectId.x-autobe-specification: Computed from hrm_platform_timelogs.project_id, mapped to hrm_platform_projects.id. SELECT project_id FROM hrm_platform_timelogs WHERE employee_id = {employeeId} GROUP BY project_id. Returns UUID of the project that the employee has logged time against.

projectName.description: Display name of the project. Retrieved from the project record to provide human-readable project identification in workload reports and dashboards.
projectName.x-autobe-specification: Computed via JOIN: SELECT projects.name FROM hrm_platform_timelogs JOIN hrm_platform_projects ON timelogs.project_id = projects.id WHERE employee_id = {employeeId} GROUP BY project_id, projects.name. Direct mapping from hrm_platform_projects.name column. Filtered to exclude soft-deleted projects (deleted_at IS NULL).

colorCode.x-autobe-specification: Computed via JOIN: SELECT projects.color_code FROM hrm_platform_timelogs JOIN hrm_platform_projects ON timelogs.project_id = projects.id WHERE employee_id = {employeeId} GROUP BY project_id, projects.color_code. Direct mapping from hrm_platform_projects.color_code column. NULL if project has no color configured - UI must handle gracefully.
colorCode.description: Color code for project visual identification in dashboards and reports. May be null if the project has no color configured.

hoursLogged.description: Total hours logged by the employee on this project. Calculated by summing all timelog durations (in minutes) for the project and converting to hours. Represents the employee's time investment in the project for workload analysis.
hoursLogged.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregation: SELECT SUM(duration_minutes) / 60.0 FROM hrm_platform_timelogs WHERE employee_id = {employeeId} GROUP BY project_id. Steps: 1) Sum all duration_minutes from timelogs for this employee and project, 2) Divide by 60 to convert minutes to hours, 3) Result is a decimal number representing total hours worked on the project. Minimum value is 0.

IHrmPlatformEmployee.IWorkloadProjectHou.description: Project-level breakdown of hours logged by an employee. Each entry represents a single project with the total hours the employee has worked on that project. Used in workload statistics to show time distribution across different projects. The hours are calculated by summing all timelog durations for the project and converting from minutes to hours. Includes project identifier, name, and color code for display purposes in dashboards and reports.
IHrmPlatformEmployee.IWorkloadProjectHou.x-autobe-specification:
Computed aggregation type combining data from hrm_platform_timelogs and hrm_platform_projects tables:

1. Data Source: hrm_platform_timelogs filtered by employee_id, grouped by project_id
2. Join: LEFT JOIN hrm_platform_projects ON timelogs.project_id = projects.id
3. Filter: Only include non-deleted projects (projects.deleted_at IS NULL)
4. Aggregation: SUM(duration_minutes) per project, divided by 60 to convert to hours
5. Sort: Results ordered by hours_logged descending in parent array

Computation Steps:
- Query hrm_platform_timelogs WHERE employee_id = {targetEmployeeId}
- GROUP BY project_id to aggregate hours per project
- SUM(duration_minutes) for each project group
- Divide sum by 60 to convert minutes to hours
- JOIN with hrm_platform_projects to retrieve project.name and project.color_code
- Filter out soft-deleted projects (deleted_at IS NULL)
- Return array of project hour breakdowns

Edge Cases:
- Empty array if employee has no timelogs
- NULL color_code handled gracefully if project has no color set
- Only includes projects where employee has logged time

employee.description: The employee who has logged the most hours on this project. Contains employee identification details including employment type, status, member account, department assignment, and role.
employee.x-autobe-specification: Transform hrm_platform_employee_id from the most active project membership to IHrmPlatformEmployee.ISummary object via JOIN on hrm_platform_employees. This represents the employee record of the team member who has logged the most hours on the project. Query joins hrm_platform_project_memberships.employee_id to hrm_platform_employees.id to retrieve employee details.

totalHoursLogged.description: Total number of hours logged by this employee on the project. Calculated as the sum of all timelog durations (in minutes) divided by 60 to convert to hours.
totalHoursLogged.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregation: SUM(duration)/60 from hrm_platform_timelogs where employee_id matches the most active team member AND project_id matches the current project AND deleted_at IS NULL. The duration field is in minutes, so divide by 60 to convert to hours. Returns a decimal number representing total hours.

totalTimelogs.description: Total number of time entries (timelogs) logged by this employee on the project. Represents the count of individual work sessions recorded.
totalTimelogs.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregation: COUNT(*) from hrm_platform_timelogs where employee_id matches the most active team member AND project_id matches the current project AND deleted_at IS NULL. Returns an integer representing the total number of time entries logged by this employee on the project.

IHrmPlatformProjectMostActiveMember.description: The most active team member on a project, representing the employee who has logged the most hours. This type provides quick identification of the top contributor without requiring clients to parse the complete team members list. Includes employee identification details and aggregated time tracking metrics (total hours logged and number of time entries).
IHrmPlatformProjectMostActiveMember.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregation type representing the most active team member on a project. Data sources: 1) Query hrm_platform_project_memberships to get all team members for the project (filter deleted_at IS NULL). 2) For each team member, aggregate from hrm_platform_timelogs: SUM(duration)/60 = totalHoursLogged, COUNT(*) = totalTimelogs. 3) Sort team members by totalHoursLogged descending. 4) Select the first member (highest hours). 5) Transform hrm_platform_employee_id to IHrmPlatformEmployee.ISummary object via JOIN on hrm_platform_employees. Return null if no team members have logged any time or if teamMembers array is empty.

employee.description: The employee assigned to this project. Contains complete employee summary including their member identity, department assignment, and role information.
employee.x-autobe-specification: Computed employee object from JOIN between hrm_platform_project_memberships and hrm_platform_employees. Returns IHrmPlatformEmployee.ISummary containing employee identity (id, employment_type, status, created_at), associated member (id, email, created_at), department (nullable), and role information. The employee is linked through project_memberships.hrm_platform_employee_id → employees.id join.

totalHoursLogged.description: Total hours logged by this team member on the project, calculated by summing all timelog durations and converting from minutes to hours.
totalHoursLogged.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregation: SUM(duration) / 60 from hrm_platform_timelogs where hrm_platform_employee_id matches the employee.id and deleted_at IS NULL. Converts total duration from minutes to hours. Returns 0 if no timelogs exist for this employee.

totalTimelogs.description: Total number of time entries (timelogs) created by this team member for the project.
totalTimelogs.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregation: COUNT(*) from hrm_platform_timelogs where hrm_platform_employee_id matches the employee.id and deleted_at IS NULL. Returns the total number of time entries created by this employee for the project. Returns 0 if no timelogs exist.

averageDailyHours.description: Average hours worked per day by this team member on the project, calculated by dividing average daily duration by the number of unique work days.
averageDailyHours.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregation: AVG(duration / 60) / COUNT(DISTINCT DATE(date)) from hrm_platform_timelogs where hrm_platform_employee_id matches the employee.id and deleted_at IS NULL. Calculates the average hours worked per unique day. Returns 0 if no timelogs exist or if COUNT(DISTINCT DATE) is 0.

lastActivityDate.description: The date of the most recent time entry for this team member on the project. Null if the employee has not yet logged any time.
lastActivityDate.x-autobe-specification: Computed aggregation: MAX(date) from hrm_platform_timelogs where hrm_platform_employee_id matches the employee.id and deleted_at IS NULL. Returns the most recent date when this employee logged time for the project. Returns null if no timelogs exist for this employee.

IHrmPlatformProjectTeamActivityMember.description: Time tracking activity summary for a single team member assigned to a project. Contains the employee's identity information along with aggregated metrics showing their total hours logged, number of time entries, average daily hours, and date of most recent activity. This data enables project leads to understand individual team member contributions and identify active contributors. Team members with no time entries are included with zero values to maintain complete team visibility.
IHrmPlatformProjectTeamActivityMember.x-autobe-specification:
Computed aggregation DTO for project team activity reporting. Query joins hrm_platform_project_memberships with hrm_platform_employees to get all team members assigned to a project, then LEFT JOINs with hrm_platform_timelogs to aggregate time tracking data per employee.

Query structure:
1. SELECT employee.id, employee.employment_type, employee.status, employee.created_at, member.id, member.email, member.created_at, department.id, department.name, role.id, role.name, role.is_builtin
2. FROM hrm_platform_project_memberships WHERE hrm_platform_project_id = {projectId} AND deleted_at IS NULL
3. JOIN hrm_platform_employees ON hrm_platform_employee_id = employees.id AND employees.deleted_at IS NULL
4. JOIN hrm_platform_members ON employees.member_id = members.id AND members.deleted_at IS NULL
5. LEFT JOIN hrm_platform_departments ON employees.department_id = departments.id AND departments.deleted_at IS NULL
6. JOIN hrm_platform_roles ON employees.role_id = roles.id AND roles.deleted_at IS NULL
7. LEFT JOIN hrm_platform_timelogs ON employees.id = timelogs.hrm_platform_employee_id AND timelogs.deleted_at IS NULL
8. GROUP BY employee.id, member.id, department.id, role.id
9. Aggregate: SUM(duration)/60 → totalHoursLogged, COUNT(*) → totalTimelogs, AVG(duration/60)/COUNT(DISTINCT DATE(date)) → averageDailyHours, MAX(date) → lastActivityDate

Edge cases handled:
- Team members with no timelogs included with 0 values and null lastActivityDate
- Only active (non-deleted) records included
- Organization context filtering implicit from authenticated user's employee record

id.description: Unique identifier for the top-level department.
id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_platform_departments.id. Primary key UUID identifier for the top-level department record.

name.description: Department name, unique within the organization.
name.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_platform_departments.name. Unique within organization scope.

description.description: Optional description clarifying the department's business purpose and responsibilities.
description.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_platform_departments.description. Nullable field providing additional context about the department's purpose and responsibilities.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the department was created.
created_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_platform_departments.created_at. ISO 8601 datetime format with timezone.

updated_at.description: Timestamp when the department was last updated.
updated_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from hrm_platform_departments.updated_at. ISO 8601 datetime format with timezone, updated on each modification.

childDepartments.description: Array of direct child departments under this top-level department. Limited to one level of nesting as per system constraints.
childDepartments.x-autobe-specification: Has-many relation from hrm_platform_departments.childDepartments. Query child departments where parent_id = this department's id. Returns array of IHrmPlatformDepartment.ISummary. Sort children by name. Only one level of nesting supported.

organization.description: The organization that owns this top-level department.
organization.x-autobe-specification: Transform hrm_platform_organization_id FK to organization object via JOIN on hrm_platform_organizations.id. Returns IHrmPlatformOrganization.ISummary containing organization details (id, name, description, owner, setting, logo, timestamps).

IHrmPlatformDepartment.ITopLevel.description:
A top-level department with its direct child departments.

This type represents a department that has no parent (top-level in the hierarchy) along with an array of its direct child departments. It is used in the department hierarchy endpoint to provide a tree structure for displaying organizational units.

The childDepartments array contains only direct children - the hierarchy is limited to one level of nesting as per system constraints. Each child department is represented as a summary with essential display information.
IHrmPlatformDepartment.ITopLevel.x-autobe-specification:
Top-level department with child departments for hierarchical display.

Direct mappings from hrm_platform_departments table:
- id: from departments.id (UUID)
- name: from departments.name (String)
- description: from departments.description (String?, nullable)
- created_at: from departments.created_at (DateTime)
- updated_at: from departments.updated_at (DateTime)

Child departments:
- childDepartments: Array of child departments where parent_id = this department's id
- Query child departments with JOIN on parent_id = parent.id
- Use IHrmPlatformDepartment.ISummary for each child department
- Sort children by name
- Only one level of nesting (children cannot have their own children in this structure)

Filter: parent_id IS NULL AND deleted_at IS NULL to get only active top-level departments.

instruction:
Generate comprehensive E2E test suites for all API endpoints of the ERP HRM & Time Tracking Platform. Tests should cover:

**Authentication & User Management Tests**
- User signup flow with unique email validation
- User login with valid/invalid credentials
- Password change flow
- Profile view and edit operations
- Organization context switching

**Organization Management Tests**
- Create organization with all required fields
- View and edit organization settings
- Delete organization (test validation: pending timesheets, active contracts)
- Multi-tenancy isolation tests

**Role & Permission Tests**
- List all roles in organization
- Create custom role with specific permissions
- Edit custom role permissions
- Delete custom role (with validation: no employees assigned)
- Assign and change employee roles

**Employee Management Tests**
- Invite employee by email (existing and new user flows)
- List employees with pagination and filters (department, employment type, status, search)
- View employee details
- Edit employee details (department, position, employment type)
- Deactivate and reactivate employees
- Verify historical data preservation after deactivation

**Contract Management Tests**
- List all contracts for an employee
- Create new contract (verify previous active contract is auto-ended)
- Edit active contract
- View contract history
- Verify historical contracts are immutable

**Department Management Tests**
- List all departments
- Create department with optional parent
- Edit department details
- Delete department (verify employees' department is set to null, not deleted)

**Project Management Tests**
- List projects with pagination and status filters
- Create project with all fields
- Edit project details
- Archive and complete projects
- Delete project (verify no timelogs exist first)
- Assign and remove employees from projects

**Task Management Tests**
- List tasks with filters (status, priority, assignee, sort options)
- Create task with all fields
- Edit task details
- Update task status (verify history is logged)
- Create subtasks (one level of nesting only)

**Timelog Tests**
- List timelogs with pagination and filters (date range, project, task, billable)
- Create timelog with all required fields
- Edit timelog (verify not in approved timesheet)
- Delete timelog (verify not in submitted/approved timesheet)
- Test permission-based access control

**Timesheet Tests**
- List timesheets with pagination and filters
- Create draft timesheet
- Add/remove timelogs from draft
- Submit timesheet (verify not empty, no duplicate week)
- Approve timesheet (verify timelogs are locked)
- Reject timesheet with reason (verifies return to draft status)

**Timer (Live Time Tracking) Tests**
- Start timer with project and optional task
- Stop timer and verify timelog creation
- Discard timer
- Edit running timer details
- Verify only one active timer per employee

**Report Generation Tests**
- Time Report with various groupings and filters
- Project Budget Report (budget vs actual hours)
- Weekly Summary Report

**Activity Log Tests**
- List activity log entries with pagination
- Filter by action type, user, date range
- Verify all significant actions are logged

**Dashboard Tests**
- Personal dashboard data accuracy
- Organization dashboard with all metrics

**Security & Authorization Tests**
- Role-based access control for each endpoint
- Organization context isolation
- Permission validation for all protected resources

Each test should include:
- Setup/teardown for test data
- Positive test cases (happy path)
- Negative test cases (invalid inputs, insufficient permissions)
- Edge cases (empty states, boundary conditions)
- Integration tests for multi-step workflows

scenario.draft: Test scenario for a new guest visitor accessing the platform for the first time. The test should verify that: 1) A new guest record is created in hrm_platform_guests table with the provided device_fingerprint, ip_address, and user_agent. 2) A corresponding session record is created in hrm_platform_guest_sessions with connection metadata (ip, href, referrer) and expiration timestamp. 3) JWT access and refresh tokens are generated and returned in the IAuthorized response format. 4) The response includes the guest's unique identifier (id) and token object with access, refresh, expired_at, and refreshable_until fields. 5) Guest session expiration times are set appropriately (shorter than member sessions). 6) The access attempt is logged for security monitoring. The test should use valid input data including a unique device fingerprint, valid IP address, and optional user agent string.

It establishes the necessary user account and authentication context for the 'guest' actor, enabling subsequent API calls that depend on this specific authorization level.
Without this join operation, the main scenario endpoint and its dependencies will fail due to insufficient authentication credentials.

functions.name: test_api_guest_join_new_device

scenario.draft: Test scenario for a returning guest visitor with the same device fingerprint. The test should be executed by calling the guest join endpoint twice with the same device_fingerprint value. The verification should confirm that: 1) When a guest with the same device_fingerprint already exists and has not been soft-deleted (deleted_at is null), the existing guest record is reused instead of creating a duplicate. 2) A new session record is created in hrm_platform_guest_sessions for the returning visit with updated connection metadata. 3) New JWT tokens are generated for the new session. 4) Both responses return the same guest id, demonstrating consistent tracking across visits. 5) The system correctly identifies the returning visitor and maintains their identity. This test validates the device fingerprint deduplication logic that ensures returning guests are tracked consistently rather than creating multiple guest records for the same device.

scenario.draft: Test the primary success path for guest token refresh. A guest who has previously registered via /hrmPlatform/auth/guest/join receives a refresh token. When the guest's access token expires, they call the refresh endpoint with their valid refresh token. The system validates the refresh token against hrm_platform_guest_sessions table, confirms the session exists and has not expired (expired_at is in the future), and generates new access and refresh tokens with updated expiration times. The response includes the guest's unique ID and new authorization tokens (access, refresh, expired_at, refreshable_until). Verify that the session's created_at timestamp is updated to the current time. This allows guests to maintain temporary access to public resources without re-registering.

scenario.draft: Test the edge case where a guest's session has expired but the guest record still exists. A guest registers via /hrmPlatform/auth/guest/join and receives tokens. After the session expires (current time is past expired_at), the guest attempts to refresh using their refresh token. The system validates that the guest record in hrm_platform_guests has not been soft-deleted (deleted_at is null), then creates a new session record in hrm_platform_guest_sessions with fresh expiration timestamps. New access and refresh tokens are generated and returned in IAuthorized format. This allows returning guests to seamlessly continue their session without re-entering device information, maintaining a smooth user experience for temporary platform access.

The guest record is then marked as deleted (deleted_at is set, simulating retention policy cleanup). When the guest attempts to refresh using their refresh token, the system validates the token against hrm_platform_guest_sessions and checks if the associated guest record in hrm_platform_guests exists and is not deleted. Since the guest record is soft-deleted, the refresh request is rejected with an appropriate error response. The guest must re-register through the join operation to obtain new access. This enforces retention policies and prevents access for guests who have been marked for cleanup.

Test successful member login when the user belongs to a single organization.

2. Include required session context fields (href, referrer, optional ip)
3. Verify HTTP 200 OK response
4. Verify response contains IHrmPlatformMember.IAuthorized structure with:
   - Member identity (id, email, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at=null)
   - JWT tokens (access, refresh, expired_at, refreshable_until)
5. Verify a session record is created in hrm_platform_member_sessions
6. Verify the access token can be used for subsequent authenticated requests
7. Verify the member's single organization is automatically set as the active context

scenario.draft:
This test validates the primary success path for administrator account registration. The test should:

1. Send a POST request to /hrmPlatform/auth/admin/join with a unique email address, valid password, href, and referrer URLs
2. Verify the response returns HTTP 201 Created status
3. Verify the response body contains the IHrmPlatformAdmin.IAuthorized structure with:
   - id: UUID string for the new administrator
   - email: The email address provided in the request
   - created_at: ISO 8601 timestamp of account creation
   - token: Object containing access, refresh, expired_at, and refreshable_until fields
4. Verify the access token is a valid JWT string
5. Verify the refresh token is a valid JWT string
6. Verify expired_at and refreshable_until are valid ISO 8601 timestamps

3. Verify the role has all three permissions assigned

Execution:
1. Call DELETE /hrmPlatform/admin/roles/{roleId}/permissions/{permissionCode} with permissionCode='employee_manage'
2. Verify HTTP 204 No Content response

Validation:
1. Verify the permission 'employee_manage' is no longer in the role's permission list
2. Verify the other permissions ('project_view', 'time_approve') remain intact
3. Verify the activity log records the permission removal event with action type 'role_permission_removed'
4. Verify all employees assigned to this role immediately lose the 'employee_manage' capability
5. Verify the permission assignment record exists with deleted_at timestamp set (soft delete)

Expected behavior:
- Permission removal succeeds for custom roles
- Soft delete preserves audit trail
- Changes propagate immediately to all role assignees

scenario.draft:
Test the primary success path for retrieving a specific task history entry by its unique identifier.

**Setup**:
1. Register and authenticate as a member user
2. Create a project within the member's organization
3. Create a task within that project with an initial status (e.g., 'todo')
4. Update the task status to a different value (e.g., 'in_progress') to automatically generate a task history entry
5. Capture the history entry ID from the task history list or task detail response

**Test Execution**:
1. Call GET /hrmPlatform/member/task-histories/{historyId} with the captured history entry ID
2. Verify the response returns HTTP 200 OK
3. Verify the response body contains IHrmPlatformTaskHistory with all required fields:
   - id: matches the requested historyId
   - task: IHrmPlatformTask.ISummary with task details (id, title, status, priority, project, etc.)
   - member: IHrmPlatformMember.ISummary with the member who made the status change (id, email)
   - old_status: the status before the change (e.g., 'todo')
   - new_status: the status after the change (e.g., 'in_progress')
   - created_at: timestamp of when the status change occurred
4. Verify the task in the response matches the task that was updated
5. Verify the member in the response matches the authenticated user who performed the update
6. Verify old_status and new_status accurately reflect the status transition
7. Verify created_at is a valid ISO 8601 datetime

**Expected Behavior**:
- The system returns complete task history entry with all status transition information
- Task and member relations are properly populated with summary data
- Timestamp accurately reflects when the status change occurred
- The immutable audit trail is correctly maintained

scenario.draft:
Test the timer list endpoint with comprehensive filtering and pagination capabilities.

**Setup**:
1. Register a new member account via /auth/member/join
2. Ensure the member has an associated employee record in an organization
3. Create at least one project in the organization
4. Create multiple timer sessions for the employee with varying states (active and stopped), different projects, and different date ranges

**Test Steps**:
1. Call PATCH /hrmPlatform/member/timers with no filters - verify returns all timers for the authenticated employee, paginated with default page size (20)
2. Call with pagination parameters (page=2, limit=10) - verify correct subset of timers is returned
3. Call with status='active' filter - verify only running timers (stopped_at IS NULL) are returned
4. Call with status='stopped' filter - verify only completed timers (stopped_at IS NOT NULL) are returned
5. Call with start_date and end_date filters - verify timers started within the date range are returned
6. Call with project_id filter - verify only timers for the specified project are returned
7. Call with task_id filter - verify only timers for the specified task are returned
8. Call with search parameter - verify timers with matching description text are returned
9. Call with sort='started_at' and order='asc' - verify timers are sorted by start time ascending
10. Call with sort='created_at' and order='desc' - verify default newest-first ordering

**Validation Points**:
- Response includes pagination metadata (current, limit, records, pages)
- Each timer summary includes: id, employee, project, task (nullable), description, started_at, stopped_at, created_at
- Data isolation is enforced - only the authenticated employee's timers are returned
- Filter combinations work correctly (e.g., status + date range)
- Empty result set returns valid pagination with records=0
- Default sorting is created_at DESC when no sort parameter provided

scenario.draft:
Test that active timers show real-time duration calculation and stopped timers show fixed duration.

**Setup**:
1. Register a new member account via /auth/member/join
2. Ensure the member has an associated employee record in an organization
3. Create at least one project in the organization
4. Start a new timer session (POST /member/timers) but do not stop it
5. Create another timer session and stop it (POST /member/timers/{timerId}/stop) to have a stopped timer

**Test Steps**:
1. Call PATCH /hrmPlatform/member/timers with status='active' filter
2. Verify the active timer is returned with stopped_at=null
3. Wait 60 seconds
4. Call PATCH /hrmPlatform/member/timers again with status='active' filter
5. Verify the same timer is returned and the duration has increased by approximately 60 seconds
6. Stop the active timer via POST /member/timers/{timerId}/stop
7. Call PATCH /hrmPlatform/member/timers with status='stopped' filter
8. Verify the timer now appears in stopped timers with a fixed stopped_at timestamp
9. Verify the duration is calculated from started_at to stopped_at (fixed value)
10. Wait another 60 seconds
11. Call PATCH /hrmPlatform/member/timers again with status='stopped' filter
12. Verify the stopped timer's duration remains unchanged (not recalculated)

**Validation Points**:
- Active timers have stopped_at=null
- Active timer duration increases over time (real-time calculation)
- Stopped timers have a fixed stopped_at timestamp
- Stopped timer duration remains constant over time
- Duration is calculated in seconds or hours as specified
- Timer transitions from active to stopped state correctly
- The original started_at timestamp is preserved when timer is stopped

scenario.draft:
Test that timer data isolation is enforced - employees can only see their own timer records.

**Setup**:
1. Register two separate member accounts (member1 and member2) via /auth/member/join
2. Ensure both members have associated employee records in the same organization
3. Create at least one project in the organization
4. As member1, create 2-3 timer sessions (both active and stopped)
5. As member2, create 2-3 timer sessions (both active and stopped)

**Test Steps**:
1. Authenticate as member1 and call PATCH /hrmPlatform/member/timers
2. Verify only member1's timers are returned (count matches member1's timer count)
3. Verify member2's timers are NOT included in the response
4. Note the timer IDs returned for member1
5. Authenticate as member2 and call PATCH /hrmPlatform/member/timers
6. Verify only member2's timers are returned (count matches member2's timer count)
7. Verify member1's timers are NOT included in the response
8. Verify the timer IDs are different from member1's response
9. As member1, try to access a specific timer ID that belongs to member2 using GET /member/timers/{timerId}
10. Verify the request is rejected with appropriate error (403 Forbidden or 404 Not Found)

**Validation Points**:
- Data isolation is enforced at the database level via employee_id filter
- Each employee can only see their own timer records
- Timer summaries include employee information for verification
- Cross-employee access attempts are blocked
- Authentication context is properly used to determine data visibility
- The filtering happens server-side, not client-side

Test that an admin can retrieve details of an active (running) timer session.

Setup:

2. Create a new timer session using POST /hrmPlatform/admin/timers with a project assignment (no task, optional description)

2. Verify the response returns HTTP 200 OK
3. Verify the response body contains IHrmPlatformTimer with all required fields:
   - id: matches the requested timer ID
   - description: matches the description provided during creation (or null if not provided)
   - started_at: timestamp when timer was started
   - stopped_at: null (timer is still running)
   - created_at: timestamp of record creation
   - updated_at: timestamp of last update
   - deleted_at: null (timer is active)
   - employee: IHrmPlatformEmployee.ISummary object with employee details
   - project: IHrmPlatformProject.ISummary object with project details
   - task: null (no task assigned in this test)

Validation Points:
- Timer status is correctly identified as running (stopped_at is null)
- Employee information is included and matches the authenticated admin's employee record
- Project information is included and matches the project assigned during timer creation
- All timestamps are in ISO 8601 format
- The response includes the complete timer entity as specified in IHrmPlatformTimer schema

Edge Cases to Consider:
- Timer with description vs timer without description
- Timer assigned to a project the admin is not a member of (admin should still have access due to elevated privileges)

scenario.draft:
Test that an admin can retrieve details of a completed (stopped) timer session.

Setup:
1. Authenticate as admin using POST /hrmPlatform/auth/admin/join
2. Create a new timer session using POST /hrmPlatform/admin/timers with a project and optional task assignment
3. Record the timer ID from the response
4. Stop the timer using PUT /hrmPlatform/admin/timers/{timerId} (or DELETE to discard, but PUT creates a timelog)

Test Execution:
1. Call GET /hrmPlatform/admin/timers/{timerId} with the recorded timer ID
2. Verify the response returns HTTP 200 OK
3. Verify the response body contains IHrmPlatformTimer with all required fields:
   - id: matches the requested timer ID
   - description: matches the description from timer creation
   - started_at: timestamp when timer was started
   - stopped_at: timestamp when timer was stopped (not null, timer is completed)
   - created_at: timestamp of record creation
   - updated_at: timestamp of last update (should match stopped_at or be close)
   - deleted_at: null (timer record is preserved)
   - employee: IHrmPlatformEmployee.ISummary object with employee details
   - project: IHrmPlatformProject.ISummary object with project details
   - task: IHrmPlatformTask.ISummary object if task was assigned, or null if not

Validation Points:
- Timer status is correctly identified as completed (stopped_at has a value)
- The duration can be calculated from started_at to stopped_at
- Employee information is included and matches the authenticated admin's employee record
- Project information is included and matches the project assigned during timer creation
- Task information is included if a task was assigned during timer creation
- All timestamps are in ISO 8601 format
- The timer record is preserved in the system (not deleted) after stopping

Business Logic Verification:
- Stopped timers are retained in the system for historical reference
- Admin can view both running and completed timers
- The timer details include complete context (employee, project, task) for audit purposes

Edge Cases to Consider:
- Timer stopped immediately after creation (very short duration)
- Timer that ran for an extended period (multiple hours or days)
- Timer with and without task assignment

Test the primary success path for timer creation where an authenticated admin employee creates a new active timer session.

Setup:
1. Authenticate as admin using /hrmPlatform/auth/admin/join
2. Create a project that the admin employee is assigned to using /hrmPlatform/member/projects

   - projectId: UUID of the project the employee is assigned to
   - taskId: UUID of a task within that project (optional)
   - description: Optional work description

Expected Results:
1. HTTP 201 Created response
2. Response body contains IHrmPlatformTimer object with:
   - id: Generated UUID for the new timer
   - started_at: Current timestamp (ISO 8601 format)
   - stopped_at: NULL (indicating timer is actively running)
   - employee: IHrmPlatformEmployee.ISummary of the authenticated admin
   - project: IHrmPlatformProject.ISummary of the selected project
   - task: IHrmPlatformTask.ISummary (if taskId provided) or null

3. Timer record is persisted in hrm_platform_timers table with:
   - hrm_platform_employee_id: Admin's employee ID from session
   - hrm_platform_project_id: Provided project ID
   - hrm_platform_task_id: Provided task ID or NULL
   - stopped_at: NULL
   - deleted_at: NULL

Validation Points:
- Timer is automatically associated with authenticated employee from session context
- started_at timestamp is set to current time
- stopped_at is NULL indicating active state
- Project assignment is validated (employee must be assigned to project)
- Task assignment is validated if provided (task must belong to selected project)
- Timer will continue running indefinitely until explicitly stopped

Test the business rule that prevents an employee from having multiple active timers simultaneously.

Setup:
1. Authenticate as admin using /hrmPlatform/auth/admin/join
2. Create a project using /hrmPlatform/member/projects

Expected Results:

2. Error response indicates that the employee already has an active timer running
3. No new timer record is created in hrm_platform_timers table
4. The original active timer remains unchanged and continues running

Validation Points:
- System queries hrm_platform_timers table for existing active timers (stopped_at IS NULL) for the authenticated employee
- Request is rejected because employee already has an active timer
- Business rule enforced: Each employee restricted to ONE active timer at any given time
- Original timer's state is preserved (not automatically stopped)
- Employee must explicitly stop or discard the existing timer before starting a new one

Edge Cases to Consider:
- Verify error message is clear and actionable
- Verify no partial state changes occur
- Verify the existing timer can still be stopped or edited normally

Test that the organization dashboard correctly identifies and displays projects exceeding their allocated budget hours.

   - overagePercentage equals 20.00 (calculated as ((120-100)/100)*100)

   - topPerformers reflects actual hours logged

**Validation Points:**
- Budget warnings only include projects where budget_hours IS NOT NULL AND actualHours > budgetHours
- Overage percentage is calculated correctly: ((actualHours - budgetHours) / budgetHours) * 100
- Projects without budget_hours (null) are excluded from warnings
- Projects within budget are excluded from warnings
- Actual hours are computed from SUM of timelog duration_hours for each project
- Budget warnings help administrators identify projects requiring attention

instruction:
Implement comprehensive business logic for all API endpoints of the ERP HRM & Time Tracking Platform. The implementation should include:

**Authentication & User Management**
- User signup with email validation and password hashing
- JWT-based authentication with organization context in tokens
- Password change with current password verification
- Profile management with avatar upload handling

**Organization Management**
- Organization creation during signup
- Settings validation (currency codes, timezone formats, fiscal month 1-12)
- Delete validation: check for pending timesheets and active employee contracts
- Cascade delete for all organization data (employees, projects, tasks, timelogs, timesheets)

**Role & Permission System**
- Built-in roles (Owner, Manager, Employee) with fixed permissions
- Custom role CRUD with permission array validation
- Role deletion validation: no employees assigned
- Permission-based authorization middleware for all endpoints

**Employee Management**
- Email invitation system with pending invitations
- Auto-add to organization on signup if pending invitation exists
- Employee CRUD with department, position, employment type management
- Deactivation logic: preserve historical data, prevent new time tracking
- Reactivation flow

**Contract Management**
- Contract creation with auto-end previous active contract logic
- Active contract editing only (historical contracts immutable)
- Pay period validation and working hours validation
- Contract date overlap prevention

**Department Management**
- Department hierarchy (one level nesting only)
- Cascade nullification of employee department on delete
- Department validation (no duplicate names in same parent)

**Project Management**
- Project CRUD with color code validation
- Archive/complete status transitions
- Delete validation: no associated timelogs
- Project member assignment with role (member/project-lead)

**Task Management**
- Task CRUD with status, priority, estimated hours
- Subtask support (one level nesting only)
- Task status change history logging
- Assignment validation (must be project member)

**Timelog Management**
- Timelog creation with project/task validation
- Edit/delete restrictions based on timesheet status
- Permission-based access control (employees own logs, managers all logs)
- Duration validation (positive minutes)

**Timesheet Management**
- Weekly timesheet generation (Monday-Sunday)
- Draft timesheet with automatic timelog inclusion
- Submit validation: not empty, no duplicate week submissions
- Approval logic: lock all timelogs
- Rejection logic: return to draft with reason
- Total hours calculation from included timelogs

**Timer (Live Time Tracking)**
- Single active timer per employee constraint
- Timer start/stop with timelog creation
- Duration rounding to nearest minute
- Timer edit while running
- Discard without creating timelog

**Report Generation**
- Time Report: aggregate hours by employee/project/task with billable breakdown
- Project Budget Report: budget vs actual with percentage calculation
- Weekly Summary: week-by-week metrics with filtering

**Activity Logging**
- Automatic logging of all significant actions
- Activity log with pagination and filtering
- Action types: employee actions, contract actions, project actions, task actions, timesheet actions, role changes

**Dashboard Data**
- Personal dashboard: today's hours, week's hours, timer status, recent timelogs, pending timesheets, assigned tasks
- Organization dashboard: employee count, total hours, pending timesheets, budget warnings, top employees

**Security & Validation**
- Organization context enforcement on every request
- Role-based authorization checks
- Input validation with proper error messages
- Soft delete where appropriate (preserve historical data)
- Hard delete only when safe (no dependencies)

**Business Rules Implementation**
- Timesheet approval locks timelogs
- Deactivated employees cannot log time
- Archived/completed projects cannot receive new timelogs
- Contract date overlap prevention
- Duplicate timesheet week prevention
- One active timer per employee

Ensure all implementations:
- Use Prisma for database operations
- Follow NestJS service patterns
- Include proper error handling
- Implement transaction support where needed
- Add comprehensive logging
- Follow the API interface specifications exactly

plan.thinking: Collects IHrmPlatformRole.ICreate to hrm_platform_roles with organization context from admin session. The DTO contains name, description, and permissions, but organization_id FK comes from authenticated admin's session context.
Collects IHrmPlatformContract.ICreate to hrm_platform_contracts. Employee organization is auto-derived from employee record.
Collects IHrmPlatformTask.ICreate to hrm_platform_tasks. Create DTO for task creation with project from path parameter and creator from authenticated member.

IHrmPlatformTaskSnapshot.ICreate maps to hrm_platform_task_snapshots. Collectable - Create DTO used for POST operations to create task snapshots. The hrm_platform_task_id FK is provided in request body, and all other FKs are denormalized from the source task during snapshot creation.

Collects IHrmPlatformTimesheet.ICreate to hrm_platform_timesheets. Employee ID resolved from authenticated member's employee record via JWT session. Only week_start_date in DTO body, employee reference comes from auth context.

Collects IHrmPlatformEmployeeInvitation.ICreate to hrm_platform_employee_invitations. The DTO contains email and role_id fields. Organization context (hrm_platform_organization_id) is derived from the authenticated admin's session, not from the DTO body.
Collects IHrmPlatformDepartment.ICreate to hrm_platform_departments with organization from auth context
Collects IHrmPlatformProject.ICreate to hrm_platform_projects with organization reference from session context
Collects IHrmPlatformProjectMembership.ICreate to hrm_platform_project_memberships. The DTO contains employee_id and role fields, but project_id is obtained from path parameter projectId.

IHrmPlatformTimer.ICreate is a Create DTO for timer sessions. Maps to hrm_platform_timers table. Employee ID is not in the DTO body - it comes from authenticated session context (member_id from JWT -> employee record). Project ID and optional task ID are provided in the request body. This is a collectable DTO requiring a collector.
Collects IHrmPlatformTimelog.ICreate to hrm_platform_timelogs. Employee ID comes from authenticated session context, not from request body.
Collects IHrmPlatformRolePermission.ICreate to hrm_platform_role_permissions. The permission_code comes from request body, but hrm_platform_role_id foreign key is obtained from path parameter roleId.
Transforms hrm_platform_organizations to IHrmPlatformOrganization.ISummary with nested owner, setting, and logo relations

IHrmPlatformOrganization maps to hrm_platform_organizations table. It's a read DTO for API responses with direct database mapping. Includes owner relation, settings, and logo as nested entities. Transformable.
Transforms hrm_platform_departments to IHrmPlatformDepartment.ISummary with nested parent (self-referential) and organization relations. Read DTO for API responses, directly database-backed.
IHrmPlatformActivityLog maps to hrm_platform_activity_logs table. It's a complete entity DTO used for API responses with nested organization, actingMember, and changes relations. Transformable.
Transforms hrm_platform_employee_invitations to IHrmPlatformEmployeeInvitation.ISummary with nested organization, role, and redeemedByMember relations. Direct mapping with FK transformations.

IHrmPlatformTask is a complete task entity DTO that maps directly to hrm_platform_tasks table. It is a read DTO for API responses with direct field mappings to database columns including id, title, description, status, priority, due_date, estimated_hours, timestamps, and foreign key relations (project, assignedEmployee, parentTask, createdByMember). The x-autobe-database-schema property explicitly specifies hrm_platform_tasks as the mapped table.

Transforms hrm_platform_timelogs to IHrmPlatformTimelog.ISummary with nested employee, project, and optional task relations. Direct mapping to hrm_platform_timelogs table with JOINs for related entities.

Transforms hrm_platform_organization_logos table to IHrmPlatformOrganizationLogo DTO. Maps id, image_url, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at directly. Transforms hrm_platform_organization_id foreign key to nested organization object (IHrmPlatformOrganization.ISummary). Read DTO with direct database mapping.
Transforms hrm_platform_timers to IHrmPlatformTimer.ISummary with nested employee, project, and task relations

IHrmPlatformTimesheetSnapshot maps to hrm_platform_timesheet_snapshots table. Transform employee FK to nested IHrmPlatformEmployee.ISummary object, transform approver_id and rejected_by_id FKs to nullable employee objects. Direct database-backed read DTO.

Transforms hrm_platform_departments to IHrmPlatformDepartment.ITopLevel with nested childDepartments array and organization relation. Direct mapping to hrm_platform_departments table where parent_id IS NULL to get top-level departments.
Transforms hrm_platform_member_sessions to IHrmPlatformMemberSession with member and organization relations via JOINs on hrm_platform_member_id and hrm_platform_organization_id
Transforms hrm_platform_guest_sessions to IHrmPlatformGuestSession.ISummary with nested guest relation from hrm_platform_guests. Read DTO for API responses, directly database-backed.
Transforms hrm_platform_organization_settings to IHrmPlatformOrganizationSetting with organization settings data including currency, timezone, and fiscal year start month

Transforms hrm_platform_employee_snapshots to IHrmPlatformEmployeeSnapshot.ISummary with nested employee, organization, member, department, and role relations. This is a Read DTO for API responses, directly mapped to the employee_snapshots table for audit trail and historical tracking of employee changes.
Transforms hrm_platform_employees with nested member, department, and role relations. Read DTO variant for API responses.

IHrmPlatformEmployee is a complete employee entity that maps directly to hrm_platform_employees database table. It's a read DTO used for API responses with direct field mappings (id, employment_type, status, timestamps) and nested relations (member, organization, department, role). The x-autobe-database-schema annotation confirms the table mapping to hrm_platform_employees.
Transforms hrm_platform_departments with parent department relation, child departments array, employee count aggregation, and organization context. Read DTO for API responses.
Transforms hrm_platform_roles to IHrmPlatformRole.ISummary with organization relation and computed aggregations (employee_count, permission_count)
Transforms hrm_platform_contracts to IHrmPlatformContract with nested employee and organization relations via JOINs. Read DTO for API responses.
Transforms hrm_platform_employee_snapshots table to IHrmPlatformEmployeeSnapshot with nested employee, organization, member, department, and role relations. Direct 1:1 mapping to database table.
Transforms hrm_platform_roles table to IHrmPlatformRole DTO with nested organization relation and permissions array from role_permissions join

Transforms hrm_platform_contract_snapshots to IHrmPlatformContractSnapshot.ISummary. Direct mapping of snapshot record fields including id, start_at, end_at, pay_rate, pay_period, working_hours_per_week, and created_at. This is a summary view for list displays in paginated results.
Transforms hrm_platform_projects to IHrmPlatformProject.ISummary for lightweight list displays. Direct mapping of project fields including id, name, status, color_code, budget_hours, and created_at.
Transforms hrm_platform_employee_invitations with organization, role, and redeemedByMember relations
Transforms hrm_platform_contract_snapshots to IHrmPlatformContractSnapshot with nested contract, employee, and organization summaries
Transforms hrm_platform_project_memberships to IHrmPlatformProjectMembership with nested employee and project relations

Transforms hrm_platform_project_snapshots to IHrmPlatformProjectSnapshot with denormalized project fields (code, name, description, status, color_code, budget_hours) and creator relation from hrm_platform_members
Transforms hrm_platform_project_memberships to IHrmPlatformProjectMembership.ISummary with employee relation mapping. Direct database-backed DTO for project membership summary responses.

Transforms hrm_platform_task_histories to IHrmPlatformTaskHistory with nested task (IHrmPlatformTask.ISummary) and member (IHrmPlatformMember.ISummary) relations. Direct field mapping for id, old_status, new_status, created_at.
Transformable DTO that maps to hrm_platform_project_snapshots table. ISummary variant for API responses with direct field mapping and nested creator relation from hrm_platform_members.

IHrmPlatformMember is a read DTO that maps directly to hrm_platform_members database table. It contains member authentication identity fields (id, email, timestamps) and is used for API responses. Transformable.

IHrmPlatformTaskHistory.ISummary maps to hrm_platform_task_histories table. This is a Read DTO used for API responses that directly maps database columns (id, old_status, new_status, created_at) and includes JOIN relations (task, member). Transformable.

Transforms hrm_platform_task_snapshots to IHrmPlatformTaskSnapshot with nested project, employee, and parentTask relations. All scalar fields are denormalized copies from source task at snapshot time.
Transforms hrm_platform_activity_log_changes to IHrmPlatformActivityLogChange.ISummary with nested activityLog relation
IHrmPlatformTimer maps to hrm_platform_timers database table. It's a read DTO used for API responses with direct field mapping and nested relations (employee, project, task). Transformable.
Transforms hrm_platform_timesheet_snapshots to IHrmPlatformTimesheetSnapshot.ISummary with employee and approver relations. Read DTO for API responses with direct database mapping.

Transformable DTO that maps to hrm_platform_activity_logs table. This is a summary variant used for displaying activity log entries in list views. The DTO directly corresponds to the hrm_platform_activity_logs database table and includes essential fields for audit trail display.

Transforms hrm_platform_tasks table to IHrmPlatformTask.ISummary with project and assigned_employee relations. Direct field mapping for id, title, status, priority, due_date, estimated_hours, created_at, updated_at, parent_task_id. JOINs to hrm_platform_projects for project relation and LEFT JOIN to hrm_platform_employees for assigned_employee relation.

IHrmPlatformTimelog maps to hrm_platform_timelogs database table. This is a transformable read DTO that represents complete time log entries with nested employee, project, and task relations. Direct field mapping for scalar columns (id, date, duration, billable, description, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at) and FK transformations for relations (employee via hrm_platform_employee_id, project via hrm_platform_project_id, task via hrm_platform_task_id).
Transforms hrm_platform_activity_log_changes table to IHrmPlatformActivityLogChange DTO with direct field mappings for audit trail change records

Transforms hrm_platform_timesheets to IHrmPlatformTimesheet with nested employee (via hrm_platform_employee_id FK) and approver (via approver_id FK) relations. Read DTO for API responses, database-backed, direct table mapping confirmed by x-autobe-database-schema field.
Transforms hrm_platform_timesheets to IHrmPlatformTimesheet.ISummary with employee and approver relations

Transforms hrm_platform_departments into hierarchical tree structure with top-level departments containing direct child departments. Queries departments table, separates into top-level (parent_id IS NULL) and child departments, then structures as nested array with one level of nesting.
Transforms hrm_platform_role_permissions table to IHrmPlatformRolePermission DTO with role relation

IHrmPlatformProject is a transformable DTO that maps 1:1 to the hrm_platform_projects table. It's a read DTO containing full project entity data including id, name, description, status, color_code, budget_hours, timestamps, and nested organization reference. The x-autobe-database-schema property explicitly points to hrm_platform_projects table, confirming direct database mapping.
Transforms hrm_platform_contracts to IHrmPlatformContract.ISummary with nested employee relation. Read DTO for API responses, DB-backed, direct mapping to hrm_platform_contracts table.

Transforms hrm_platform_task_snapshots to IHrmPlatformTaskSnapshot.ISummary with nested project, employee, parentTask, and creatorSession relations. All scalar fields map directly from database columns. FK columns transformed to relation objects.
Transforms hrm_platform_guests table to IHrmPlatformGuest.ISummary with direct field mapping for guest visitor information including device fingerprint, IP address, and timestamps
Transforms hrm_platform_members to IHrmPlatformMember.ISummary with id, email, and created_at fields. Lightweight summary variant for identity references across the platform.
Transforms hrm_platform_member_sessions to IHrmPlatformMemberSession.ISummary with nested member and organization relations. Read DTO for API responses, directly maps to database table.
